header.Title (Source): King Arthur - Sword in the Stone

text.S1: LONG, long ago, after Uther Pendragon died, there was no King in Britain, and every Knight hoped to seize the crown for himself. The country was likely to fare ill when laws were broken on every side, and the corn which was to give the poor bread was trodden underfoot, and there was none to bring the evildoer to justice.
text.S2: LONG, long ago, after Uther Pendragon died, there was no King in Britain, and every Knight hoped to seize the crown for himself. text.T1: KALE, kale, pambuyo pa imfa ya Uther Pendragon, dziko la Britain linali lopanda Mfumu, ndipo Munthu aliyense Wolemekezeka anali ndi ciyembekezo codzakhala mfumu iyeyo. Dziko silinali kuyenda bwino pomwe malamulo anaphwanyidwa pa mbali iliyonse, ndipo cimanga comwe cimati cidzagwiritsidwe nchito kupatsa osauka kuti azipangira buledi cinapondedwapondedwa, ndipo panalibe aliyense yemwe akanapereka wolakwayo ku ciweruzo.
text.T2: KALE, kale, pambuyo pa imfa ya Uther Pendragon, dziko la Britain linali lopanda Mfumu, ndipo Msilikari aliyense wolemekezeka anali ndi ciyembekezo codzakhala mfumu iyeyo. Dziko silinali kuyenda bwino pomwe malamulo anaphwanyidwa pa mbali iliyonse, ndipo cimanga comwe cimati cidzagwiritsidwe nchito kupatsa osauka kuti azipangira buledi cinapondedwapondedwa, ndipo panalibe aliyense yemwe akanapereka wolakwayo ku ciweruzo.

text.S1: Then, when things were at their worst, came forth Merlin the magician, and fast he rode to the place where the Archbishop of Canterbury had his dwelling. And they took counsel together, and agreed that all the lords and gentlemen of Britain should ride to London and meet on Christmas Day, now at hand, in the Great Church. So, this was done. And on Christmas morning, as they left the church, they saw in the churchyard a large stone, and on it a bar of steel, and in the steel a naked sword was held, and about it was written in letters of gold, ‘Whoso pulleth out this sword is by right of birth King of England.’
text.S2: Then, when things were at their worst, came forth Merlin the magician, and fast he rode to the place where the Archbishop of Canterbury had his dwelling. text.T1: Pambuyo pake, pomwe zinthu zinafika poipa kwambiri, kuanadzabwera Merlin, munthu wamatsenga, ndipo iyeyo anakwera hosi lake mofulumira kupita kumalo komwe m’busa Archbishop wa Canterbury amakhala. Awiriwo analandira uphungu pamodzi, ndipo anagwirizana kuti azimbuye onse pamodzi ndi azibambo a dziko la Britain ayenera kukwera mahosi awo kupita kumzinda wa London ndi kukakumana kumeneko pa Tsiku la Khirisimasi, limene linali pafupi kwambiri, M’chalichi Cacikulu. Conco zimenezi zinacitika. Ndipo patsiku la Khirirsimasi m’mawa, pomwe amatuluka m’chalichi, iwo anaona mwala waukulu m’bwalo la chalichi, ndipo pamwalapo panali citsulo colimba, ndipo m’kati mwake mwa citsuloco munali lupanga losungidwa, ndipo pa lupangapo panalembedwa malembo a golide, ‘Aliyense yemwe adzguza kucotsa lupanga ili, adzakhala mbadwa ya Ufumu wa England.’

text.S1: They marveled at these words, and called for the Archbishop, and brought him into the place where the stone stood. Then those Knights who fain would be King could not hold themselves back, and they tugged at the sword with all their might; but it never stirred. The Archbishop watched them in silence, but when they were faint from pulling he spoke: ‘The man is not here who shall lift out that sword, nor do I know where to find him. But this is my counsel—that two Knights be chosen, good and true men, to keep guard over the sword.’

text.T1: Iwo anadawa ndi mau awa, ndipo anaitana Bishopo Wamkulu, ndikum’pereka komwe kunali mwala. Ndiye asilikari wolemekezeka aja amene amafunitsitsa kudzakhala Mfumu sakanadziletsa kum’cirikiza, ndipo iwo anaguza lupanga lija ndi mphamvu zawo zonse; koma silinasunthe. Bishopo Wamkulu anapenyetsetsa mwakacetecete, komapomwe iwo anafooka ndi kuguza iye analankhula naati: ‘Palibe munthu pano yemwe adzacotsa lupanga, ngakhale ine sindidziwa kom’peza. Komauphungu wanga ndi uwu—kuti Olemekezeka awiri asankhidwe, amuna abwino ndi oona, kuti ayang’anire pa lupanga ili.’

text.S1: Thus it was done. But the lords and gentlemen-at-arms cried out that every man had a right to try to win the sword, and they decided that on New Year’s Day a tournament should be held, and any Knight who would, might enter the lists.

text.T1: Zinacitidwa motero. Koma azimbuye ndi azibambo ausilikari anadandaula kuti munthu aliyense ali ndi ufulu woyesa kutenga lupanga, ndipo iwo anaganiza kuti mpikisanowo ukacitikire pa Tsiku la Nyuwele, ndipo Wolemekezeka aliyense amene angafune, angalowe nawo pamndandanda.

text.S1: So on New Year’s Day, the Knights, as their custom was, went to hear service in the Great Church, and after it was over they met in the field to make ready for the tourney. Among them was a brave Knight called Sir Ector, who brought with him Sir Kay, his son, and Arthur, Kay’s foster-brother. Now Kay had unbuckled his sword the evening before, and in his haste to be at the tourney had forgotten to put it on again, and he begged Arthur to ride back and fetch it for him. But when Arthur reached the house the door was locked, for the women had gone out to see the tourney, and though Arthur tried his best to get in he could not.

text.T1: Conco patsiku la New Year’s Day, Olemekezeka, monga mmene mwambo wawo unlili, anapita kukamvetsera ku mapemphero a m’Chalichi Cacikulu, ndipo pambuyo pake iwo anakumana m’munda kukonzekera za mpikisanowo. Pakati pawo panali munthu Wolemekezeka wolimba mtima wochedwa Bambo Ector, amene anabweranso ndi Abambo Kay, mwana wawo, ndi Arthur, m’bale wopeza wa Kay. Podzafika pano, Kay anali atamasula lamba wa lupanga lake madzulo apitawo, ndipo cifukwa cofulumira kudzapezeka pa mpikisano anali ataiwala kuuvalanso lamba wakewo, ndipo iye anapempha Arthur kuti akwerenso hosi ndi kukamufuna iye. Koma pamene Arthur anafika panyumba, anapeza kuti citseko ndi cotseka, cifukwa azimai anali atapita kumpikisano, ndipo ngakhale kuti Arthur anayetsetsa kulowa sanathe kucita tero.

text.S1: Then he rode away in great anger, and said to himself, ‘Kay shall not be without a sword this day. I will take that sword in the churchyard, and give it to him’; and he galloped fast till he reached the gate of the churchyard. Here he jumped down and tied his horse tightly to a tree, then, running up to the stone, he seized the handle of the sword, and drew it easily out; afterwards he mounted his horse again, and delivered the sword to Sir Kay. The moment Sir Kay saw the sword he knew it was not his own, but the sword of the stone, and he sought out his father Sir Ector, and said to him, ‘Sir, this is the sword of the stone, therefore I am the rightful King.’

text.T1: Pambuyo ake, iye anakweranso hosi yake mwaukali, ndipo anati mumtima mwake, lf, ‘Kay sadzakhala wopanda lupanga kufikira lero. Ndidzatenga lupanga lomwe lili mu mpanda wa chalichi, ndi kum’patsa iye’; ndipo anakweranso hosi ndipo inathamanga kwambiri mpaka kukafika pacipata ca mpanda wa chalichi. Atafika, iye analumphira pansi ndi kumangirira cingwe ca hosi yake kumtengo, ndipo, atathamangira kumwala, anagwira cogwirira lupanga, ndi kutcotsa lupangalo mosavuta; pambuyo pake, iye anakweranso hosi yake, ndi kukapereka lupanga kwa Abambo Kay. Pa nthawi imene Abambo Kay anaona lupanga anadziwa kuti silinali lupanga lawo, koma lupanga lamwala, ndipo anafunafuna atate ake Abambo Ector, ndipo anati kwa iwo, ‘Abambo, ili ndi ndi lupanga lamwala, cotero ndine woyenera kukhala Mfumu.’

Ndidzatenga lupanga lomwe lili mu mpanda wa chalichi, ndi kum’patsa iye’; ndipo anakweranso hosi ndipo inathamanga kwambiri mpaka kukafika pacipata ca mpanda wa chalichi. Pa nthawi imene Abambo Kay anaona lupanga anadziwa kuti silinali lupanga lawo, koma lupanga lamwala, ndipo anafunafuna atate ake Abambo Ector, ndipo anati kwa iwo, ‘Abambo, ili ndi ndi lupanga lamwala, cotero ndine woyenera kukhala Mfumu.’

text.S1: Sir Ector made no answer, but signed to Kay and Arthur to follow him, and they all three went back to the church. Leaving their horses outside, they entered the choir, and here Sir Ector took a holy book and bade Sir Kay swear how he came by that sword. ‘My brother Arthur gave it to me,’ replied Sir Kay. ‘How did you come by it?’ asked Sir Ector, turning to Arthur. ‘Sir,’ said Arthur, ‘when I rode home for my brother’s sword I found no one to deliver it to me, and as I resolved he should not be swordless I thought of the sword in this stone, and I pulled it out.’ ‘Were any Knights present when you did this?’ asked Sir Ector. ‘No, none,’ said Arthur. ‘Then it is you,’ said Sir Ector, ‘who are the rightful King of this land.’

text.T1: Abambo Ector sanayankhe, koma anangouza Kay ndi Arthur kuti awalondole iwo, ndipo atatuwo anabwerera kuchalichi. Atasiya mahosi awo panja, iwo analowa m’chalichi momwe amaimba nyimbo, ndipo munumo Abambo Ector anatenga buku lopatulika ndipo anaitana Abambo Kay kulumbira momwe anapezera lupanga lija. ‘M’bale wanga Arthur anandipatsa ine lupanga ili,’ anayankha tero Bambo Kay. ‘Kodi munalipeza bwanji?’ anafunsa Abambo Ector, akutembenukira kwa Arthur. ‘Abambo,’ anayankhula Arthur, ‘pamene ndinakwera hosi kukatenga lupanga la m’bale wanga, ndinapeza kuti panalibe aliyense amene akanandibweretsera lupanga limenelo, cifukwa ndinali nditatsimikiza kuti sayenera kukhala wopanda lupanga, ndinaganiza za lupanga limene linali m’mwala uwu, ndipo ndinaliguza kulicotsa.’ ‘Kodi pali Olemekezeka aliyense pomwe unacita cimeneci?’ anafunsa Abambo Ector. ‘Iai, panalibe aliyense,’ anatero Arthur. ‘Pambuyo pake, Abambo’ Ector anati, ‘iweyo, ndiye amene woyenera kukhala Mfumu ya dziko lino.’

text.S1: ‘But why am I the King?’ inquired Arthur. ‘Because,’ answered Sir Ector, ‘this is an enchanted sword, and no man could draw it but he who was born a King. Therefore, put the sword back into the stone, and let me see you take it out.’ ‘That is soon done,’ said Arthur, replacing the sword, and Sir Ector himself tried to draw it, but he could not. ‘Now it is your turn,’ he said to Sir Kay, but Sir Kay fared no better than his father, though he tugged with all his might and main. ‘Now you, Arthur,’ and Arthur pulled it out as easily as if it had been lying in its sheath, and as he did so Sir Ector and Sir Kay sank on their knees before him.

text.T1: ‘Koma, n’cifukwa ciyani ndine Mfumu?’ anafunsa Arthur. ‘Cifukwa,’ anayankha Abambo Ector, ‘limeneli ndi lupanga lamatsenga, ndipo palibe munthu aliyense amene akanalitulutsa koma yekhayo yemwe anabadwa kudzakhala Mfumu. Cotero, ikaninso lupanga limeneli m’mwala, ndipo ndifuna kuti ndikuone ukulitulutsa.’ ‘Cimeneco cicitidwa posacedwa,’ anatero Arthur, akubwezera lupanga m’mwala, ndipo Abambo Ector eniake anayesa kulicotsa lupanga lija koma analephera. ‘Tsopano ndi mpata wako wakuti ucotse lupanga,’ anatero Bambo Kay, komanso Bambo Kay analephera ngati atate awo, ngakhale kuti anaguza ndi mphamvu zawo zonse. ‘Tsopano ndiwe, Arthur,’ ndipo Arthur anangoguza mosavuta ngati kuti lupanga limenelo linali m’cimake, ndipo pamenepo Abambo Ector ndi Bambo Kay anagwada pa mawondo awo pamaso pake.

text.S1: ‘Why do you, my father and brother, kneel to me?’ asked Arthur in surprise. ‘Nay, nay, my lord,’ answered Sir Ector, ‘I was never your father, though till to-day I did not know who your father really was. You are the son of Uther Pendragon, and you were brought to me when you were born by Merlin himself, who promised that when the time came I should know from whom you sprang. And now it has been revealed to me.’ But when Arthur heard that Sir Ector was not his father, he wept bitterly. ‘If I am King,’ he said at last, ‘ask what you will, and I shall not fail you. For to you, and to my lady and mother, I owe more than to anyone in the world, for she loved me and treated me as her son.’ ‘Sir,’ replied Sir Ector, ‘I only ask that you make your foster-brother, Sir Kay, Seneschal¹ of all your lands.’ ‘That I will readily,’ answered Arthur, ‘and while he and I live no other shall fill that once.’

text.T1: ‘N’cifukwa ciyani, inu atate ndi m’bale wanga mukundigwadira?’ aanafunsa modabwa Arthur. ‘Iai, iai, mbuye wanga,’ anayankha Abambo Ector, ‘Sindinali atate ako, kufikira lero, sindinadziwe kwenikweni amene atate ako anali. Iwe ndiwe mwana wamwamuna wa Uther Pendragon, ndipo unabweretsedwa kwa ine ndi Merlin mwiniwake pomwe unabadwa, amene analonjeza kuti nthawi ikadzafika ndikadziwe kumene unacokera. Tsopano cinsinsi cavumbulutsidwa kwa ine.’ Koma pomwe Arthur anamva zakuti Abambo Ector sanali atate ake, analira mopweteka mtima. ‘Ngati ndine Mfumu,’ anati potsirizira, ‘ndipempheni ciliconse cimene mufuna, ndipo sindidzalephera kukupatsani. Kwa inu, pamodzi ndi amai anga, ndili ndi ngongole yaikulu koposa aliyense m’dziko, cifukwa amai amandikonda ndi kundisunga ngati mwana wawo.’ ‘Bambo,’ anayankha Abambo Ector, ‘ndingokupempha kuti Bambo Kay akhale m’bale wako wopeza, Seneschal¹ ndi madera anu ena onse.’ ‘Zimenezo zidzakhala tero,’ anayankha Arthur, ‘ndipo pamene iye ali moyo pamodzi nane palibe wina amene adzakwanitsa zimenezo nthawi imodzi.’

Iwe ndiwe mwana wamwamuna wa Uther Pendragon, ndipo unabweretsedwa kwa ine ndi Merlin mwiniwake pomwe unabadwa, amene analonjeza kuti nthawi ikadzafika ndikadziwe kumene unacokera. Tsopano cinsinsi cavumbulutsidwa kwa ine.’ Koma pomwe Arthur anamva zakuti Abambo Ector sanali atate ake, analira mopweteka mtima. ‘Ngati ndine Mfumu,’ anati potsirizira, ‘ndipempheni ciliconse cimene mufuna, ndipo sindidzalephera kukupatsani. Kwa inu, pamodzi ndi amai anga, ndili ndi ngongole yaikulu koposa aliyense m’dziko, cifukwa amai amandikonda ndi kundisunga ngati mwana wawo.’ ‘Bambo,’ anayankha Abambo Ector, ‘ndingokupempha kuti Bambo Kay m’bale wako wopeza, akhale Seneschal¹ ndi madera anu ena onse.’ ‘Zimenezo zidzakhala tero,’ anayankha Arthur, ‘ndipo pamene iye ali moyo pamodzi nane palibe wina amene adzakwanitsa zimenezo nthawi iliyonse.’

text.S1: Sir Ector then made them seek out the Archbishop with him, and they told him all that had happened concerning the sword, which Arthur had left standing in the stone. And on the Twelfth Day the Knights and Barons came again, but none could draw it out but Arthur. When they saw this, many of the Barons became angry and cried out that they would never own a boy for a King whose blood was no better than their own. So it was agreed to wait till Candlemas, when more Knights might be there, and meanwhile the same two men who had been chosen before watched the sword night and day; but at Candlemas it was the same thing, and at Easter. And when Pentecost came, the common people who were present, and saw Arthur pull out the sword, cried with one voice that he was their King, and they would kill any man who said differently. Then all around fell on their knees before him, and Arthur took the sword and offered it upon the altar where the Archbishop stood, and the best man that was there made him Knight. After that the crown was put on his head, and he swore to his lords and commons that he would be a true King, and would do them justice all the days of his life.

text.T1: Pambuyo pake, Abambo Ector pamodzi nawo, anawacititsa kufunafuna M’busa Wamkulu, ndipo anamuuza zonse zimene zinacitika zokhudza lupanga, limene Arthur anali atalisiya m’mwala. Ndipo pa Tsiku Lacikhumi ndi Ciwiri Olemekekezeka ndi Mafumu anabweranso, koma panalibe ngakhale m’modzi yemwe akanatulutsa lupanga koma Athur cabe. Pamene iwo anaona cimeneci, Mafumu ambiri anakwiya ndipo anadandaula kuti sangalemekeze mnyamata kukhala Mfumu yemwe magazi ake sanali osiyana ndi magazi awo. Conco, onse anagwirizana kuti ayembekezere Candlemas, pomwe Olemekezeka angakhalepo, ndipo pa nthawiyo amuna awiri aja omwe anasankhidwa poyamba amayang’anira lupanga usana ndi usiku; koma pa Candlemas paja zinthu zinali cimodzimodzi, ngati panthawi ya Easter. Ndipo pamene Pentekosite inakwana, anthu wamba amene analipo, anaona Arthur akuguza lupanga, anakweza liu lawo pamodzi ndi kuti iye ndiye anali Mfumu yawo, ndipo kuti adzapha munthu aliyense yemwe akananena mosiyana. Ndiye pambuyo pake, anthu onse anagwada pamawondo awo kum’gwadira iye, ndipo Arthur anatenga lupanga ndi kulipereka paguwa lansembe pomwe anaimirira M’busa Wamkulu, ndipo munthu wabwino amene anali pamenepo anaikidwa kukhala Munthu Wolemekezeka. Pambuyo pake, cisoti cacifumu cinaikidwa pamutu pake, ndipo analumbira kwa azimbuye ndi kwa anthu onse kuti adzakhaladi Mfumu yoona, ndipo adzawaweruza mwacilungamo masiku onse a moyo wake
text.T2: Pambuyo pake, Abambo Ector pamodzi nawo, anawacititsa kufunafuna M’busa Wamkulu, ndipo anamuuza zonse zimene zinacitika zokhudza lupanga, limene Arthur anali atalisiya m’mwala. Ndipo pa Tsiku Lacikhumi ndi Ciwiri Asilikari olemekekezeka ndi Mafumu anabweranso, koma panalibe ngakhale m’modzi yemwe akanatulutsa lupanga koma Arthur cabe. Pamene iwo anaona cimeneci, Mafumu ambiri anakwiya ndipo anadandaula kuti sangalemekeze mnyamata kukhala Mfumu yemwe magazi ake sanali osiyana ndi magazi awo. Conco, onse anagwirizana kuti ayembekezere misa yamakhendulo, pomwe asilikari olemekezeka angakhalepo, ndipo pa nthawiyo amuna awiri aja omwe anasankhidwa poyamba amayang’anira lupanga usana ndi usiku; koma pa misa yamakhendulo paja zinthu zinali cimodzimodzi, ngati panthawi ya Pasaka. Ndipo pamene Pentekosite inakwana, anthu wamba amene analipo, anaona Arthur akuguza lupanga, anakweza liu lawo pamodzi ndi kuti iye ndiye anali Mfumu yawo, ndipo kuti adzapha munthu aliyense yemwe akananena mosiyana. Ndiye pambuyo pake, anthu onse anagwada pamawondo awo kum’gwadira iye, ndipo Arthur anatenga lupanga ndi kulipereka paguwa lansembe pomwe anaimirira M’busa Wamkulu, ndipo munthu wabwino amene anali pamenepo anaikidwa kukhala Munthu Wolemekezeka. Pambuyo pake, cisoti cacifumu cinaikidwa pamutu pake, ndipo analumbira kwa azimbuye ndi kwa anthu onse kuti adzakhaladi Mfumu yoona, ndipo adzawaweruza mwacilungamo masiku onse a moyo wake.
